title_en: Sichuan Jinhe Mining Co., Ltd. v. Xinjiang Lingang Resources Investment Co., Ltd. — dispute over special area cooperative exploration contract
ruling_gist_en: The contractual agreement of the parties concerning the exploration and extraction of mineral resources in areas such as nature reserves, scenic spots, key ecological function areas, ecologically sensitive areas, and ecologically fragile areas shall not violate the mandatory provisions of laws and administrative regulations or harm the public interest in the environment; otherwise, it shall be determined null and void in accordance with the law. Even if the prohibitive provisions in environmental and resource laws and regulations do not explicitly state that a violation will lead to the invalidity of the contract, if recognizing the contract as valid and continuing to perform it would harm the public interest in the environment, the contract shall be determined null and void.
keywords_en: civil; contract dispute; second instance; Supreme People's Court; Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; Sichuan Province; legal person; Contract Law; contract validity; prohibitive provisions of nature reserves; environmental public interest; dismissal of claims; cooperative exploration of mining rights; nature reserve; contract invalidity; protection of environmental public interest; dispute over cooperative exploration contracts in special areas
full_text_en:
Sichuan Jinhe Mining Co., Ltd. v. Xinjiang Lingang Resource Investment Co., Ltd. — dispute over a cooperation exploration contract in special areas

【Ruling Summary】

The parties' contractual agreement on exploration and mining of mineral resources within areas such as nature reserves, scenic spots, key ecological function zones, ecologically sensitive and fragile zones shall not violate the mandatory provisions of laws and administrative regulations or harm the environmental public interest; otherwise, it shall be determined null and void in accordance with law. Even if a prohibitive provision in environmental and resource laws and regulations does not explicitly state that a contract violating such provision will be invalid, if upholding the contract as valid and allowing its continued performance would harm the environmental public interest, the contract shall be determined null and void.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2015) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 167

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance, Counterclaim Plaintiff): Xinjiang Lingang Resource Investment Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room 1, 35th Floor, Zhongtian Plaza, No. 165 Xinhua North Road, Tianshan District, Urumqi, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region.

Legal Representative: Xu Xiangdong, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Li Yong, Attorney at Beijing Junhe Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zheng Yuejie, Attorney at Beijing Junhe Law Firm.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance, Counterclaim Defendant): Sichuan Jinhe Mining Co., Ltd. Domicile: Longtan Industrial Park, Section 2 of East Third Ring Road, Chenghua District, Chengdu, Sichuan Province.

Legal Representative: Pan Yanghui, General Manager.

Agent ad litem: Liu Bing, Staff of the company.

Agent ad litem: Deng Xueqiang, Attorney at Sichuan Mingju Law Firm.

The appellant, Xinjiang Lingang Resource Investment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Lingang Company), appealed to this court against the civil judgment (2014) Xin Min Er Chu Zi No. 13 rendered by the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region in the case of contract dispute with the appellee, Sichuan Jinhe Mining Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jinhe Company). This court formed a collegial panel in accordance with law and held a public hearing on August 18, 2015. Xu Xiangdong, the legal representative of Lingang Company, and its agents ad litem Li Yong and Zheng Yuejie, as well as the agents ad litem of Jinhe Company, Liu Bing and Deng Xueqiang, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. This case has now been concluded.

The facts found by the court of first instance upon trial:

On October 10, 2011, Lingang Company (Party A) and Jinhe Company (Party B) signed the "Agreement on Cooperation Exploration and Development of the General Survey Exploration Right of the Wuruke Lead Polymetallic Ore in Taxkorgan County, Xinjiang" (hereinafter referred to as the "Cooperation Exploration and Development Agreement"). The parties agreed that after Party A compensates Party B RMB 35,000,000, Party B is willing to inject its general survey exploration right of the Wuruke Lead Polymetallic Ore in Taxkorgan County, Xinjiang (hereinafter referred to as the "mining right") into a project company to be established by both parties, subject to the consideration and other terms and conditions stipulated in this agreement. The project company is to be jointly established by Party A with cash contribution and Party B with the mining right contribution, with a registered capital tentatively set at RMB 10,000,000, of which Party A holds 80% and Party B holds 20%. Thereafter, Party A shall fund the general survey, detailed survey, and exploration work for the mine, and the relevant results shall be owned by the project company, while the relevant risks shall be borne by the project company. Before the transfer procedures for the subject mining right are completed, Party A entrusts Party B to hold the mining right on its behalf. When the conditions for transferring the subject mining right are met, Party B shall directly transfer the subject mining right to the project company. Before the transfer procedures are completed, Party B shall be responsible for maintaining the subject mining right, including but not limited to extending the validity period of the mining certificate, annual inspection, and submitting relevant materials to the relevant authorities. After this agreement takes effect, the subsequent general survey, detailed survey, and exploration work for the subject mining right shall all be funded by Party A. Before the exploration phase is completed, Party B shall no longer invest funds. The results of the exploration work funded by Party A shall be owned by the project company. Party A's payment of the cooperation compensation for the subject mining right to Party B and its injection of subsequent exploration funds into the project company are inseparable parts of, and mutually conditional with, Party B's transfer of the subject mining right to the project company and the cooperative development. Within 15 days after the agreement is signed, Party A shall pay a deposit of RMB 35,000,000 in a lump sum to the account designated by Party B. On the date when the registration procedures for transferring the subject mining right to the project company are completed, the deposit shall be directly converted into the cooperation compensation payment made by Party A to Party B for the mining right. Both parties shall bear their respective taxes and levies arising from the conclusion and performance of this agreement in accordance with laws and regulations. The costs and expenses incurred in preparing, concluding, and performing this agreement, as well as expenses and expenditures other than taxes arising from the mining right mentioned in this agreement, shall be equally shared by Party A and Party B. Party B warrants and represents to Party A: Party B first obtained the preliminary exploration right for the Wuruke Lead Polymetallic Ore in Taxkorgan County, Xinjiang, issued by the Department of Land and Resources of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region on December 30, 2008. On January 26, 2011, it was regularly renewed and upgraded to a general survey right, now named the General Survey Exploration Right of the Wuruke Lead Polymetallic Ore in Taxkorgan County, Xinjiang, with Exploration License No.: T65120081202022682, a mining area of 31.28 square kilometers, and a validity period from January 26, 2011, to January 26, 2013. Party B warrants that the above-obtained exploration permit has clear and complete ownership, no other disputes over rights, and no existing mortgages or similar encumbrances. This exploration permit meets the legal conditions for acquisition and possesses the rights and permissions required by national laws and local regulations. There are no uncertain matters such as possible revocation of the Exploration License by the land and resources management department, and it is not located within glacier protection areas, nature reserves, scenic spots, or other areas that may affect mining development. Party A warrants and represents to Party B: Party A warrants to accelerate the exploration work of the subject mining right after the signing of this agreement. Party A warrants to fully fund the subsequent general survey, detailed survey, and exploration phases of the subject mining right. After the exploration phase of the mine is completed, subsequent investment funds shall be borne by all shareholders in proportion to their equity interests. The occurrence of any of the following events constitutes a breach of contract by that party: any party violates any term of this agreement; any party violates any representation, warranty, or undertaking made in this agreement, or any representation, warranty, or undertaking made by any party in this agreement is found to be untrue, inaccurate, or misleading; a party, without obtaining prior consent from the other party, directly or indirectly sells the subject mining right it holds to a third party; if any party breaches the contract, the other party is entitled to demand immediate termination of this agreement and/or claim liability for breach of contract in accordance with legal provisions, and to seek compensation for all losses incurred thereby (including but not limited to litigation costs, attorney fees, etc.). This agreement shall be terminated or rescinded for the following reasons: if this agreement cannot be performed due to force majeure, it shall be terminated after written confirmation by both parties; if both parties agree to terminate this agreement by mutual consent; if one party materially breaches this agreement, making it impossible for the other party to achieve the purpose of the agreement, the non-breaching party is entitled to rescind this agreement. Additionally, the parties also agreed on other matters such as confidentiality and notifications. This agreement shall take effect upon signing and sealing by both parties.

On October 25, 2011, Lingang Company paid RMB 35,000,000 to Jinhe Company by bank transfer, and Jinhe Company issued a receipt to it.

On April 28, 2012, Lingang Company signed the "Geological Exploration Project Contract" with the Sichuan Nuclear Industry Geological Survey Institute (hereinafter referred to as the Geological Survey Institute). The contract stipulated: Lingang Company commissioned the Geological Survey Institute to conduct geological exploration of the Wuruke Iron Polymetallic Ore in Taxkorgan County, Xinjiang, and to submit final review results reports, original materials, results, related maps, and electronic documents. The ownership of all materials belongs to Lingang Company, and the Geological Survey Institute shall not disclose them to any third party. Contract period: from December 20, 2011, to December 30, 2012. Contract price: budgeted contract price of RMB 10,960,500. Additionally, the parties also agreed on matters such as settlement and payment, technical standards and requirements, liability for breach, modification and termination of the contract, and dispute resolution. This contract has been actually performed.

On July 1, 2013, Lingang Company signed the "Geological Exploration Project Contract" with the Geological Survey Institute. The contract stipulated: Lingang Company commissioned the Geological Survey Institute to conduct geological exploration of the Wuruke Iron Polymetallic Ore in Taxkorgan County, Xinjiang, and to submit the final review results report and all complete original materials. All original materials, results, reports, and electronic documents formed by the exploration work shall belong to Lingang Company, and the Geological Survey Institute shall not disclose them to any third party. Contract period: from January 1, 2013, to December 30, 2013. Contract price: budgeted contract price of RMB 10,484,200. Additionally, the parties also agreed on matters such as settlement and payment, technical standards and requirements, liability for breach, modification and termination of the contract, and dispute resolution.

On July 23, 2013, Taxkorgan County Jinhe Kunlun Resource Investment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the project company) was established.

On November 22, 2013, Lingang Company issued to Jinhe Company the "Letter on the Rescission of the Agreement on Cooperation Exploration and Development of the General Survey Exploration Right of the Wuruke Lead Polymetallic Ore in Taxkorgan County, Xinjiang" (hereinafter referred to as the "Letter of Rescission"). The main content was: Recently, Lingang Company was shocked to learn from relevant authorities that the cooperative development project involved is located in the central area of the Xinjiang Taxkorgan Wildlife Nature Reserve (hereinafter referred to as the "Reserve"), which Jinhe Company had not informed Lingang Company of since the cooperation began. According to Articles 6 and 7 of the Cooperation Exploration and Development Agreement, Jinhe Company's conduct constitutes a breach of contract. To perform the agreement, Lingang Company had paid a cooperation deposit of RMB 35,000,000 to Jinhe Company and invested approximately RMB 17,000,000 in mine road construction, mine construction, geological exploration, road access fees, and other projects, with related capital costs amounting to nearly RMB 10,000,000. After study, Lingang Company decided to terminate the cooperation and rescind the Cooperation Exploration and Development Agreement signed between the parties, and expected Jinhe Company to bear the corresponding liability in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Cooperation Exploration and Development Agreement.

On December 30, 2013, Jinhe Company issued to Lingang Company the "Reply on Continuing to Perform the Agreement on Cooperation Exploration and Development of the General Survey Exploration Right of the Wuruke Lead Polymetallic Ore in Taxkorgan County, Xinjiang" (hereinafter referred to as the "Reply"). The main content was: The Letter of Rescission from Lingang Company has been received. After verification with relevant authorities, the Reserve had already been established before Jinhe Company first obtained the mining right on December 26, 2008. From December 30, 2008, to January 26, 2011, the mining right passed the regular annual inspections of the Autonomous Region Department of Land and Resources and was renewed and upgraded to a general survey. After the two parties signed the Cooperation Exploration and Development Agreement and began cooperative exploration, the mining right was again regularly renewed on April 9, 2013, spanning nearly five years (including over two years of cooperative exploration). During this period, no department or agency informed Jinhe Company about the matter of the Reserve, and the exploration work of the mining right during the over two years of cooperation was not affected in any way. Therefore, it is not the case that Jinhe Company knew the mining right was located in the Reserve and concealed it from Lingang Company. Precisely because Jinhe Company was not aware of the foregoing situation, it accepted the clause regarding "representations and warranties" about the Reserve in Article 6 of the text of the cooperation exploration agreement provided by Lingang Company. Due to asymmetry in access to information about the Reserve, combined with the fact that the mining right was legally obtained and regularly renewed and inspected, neither party noticed the foregoing situation when concluding and performing the Cooperation Exploration and Development Agreement. Jinhe Company did not know the mining right was located in the Reserve and conceal it from Lingang Company, much less would it make an unfavorable warranty in the agreement while knowing such fact. The mining right, from its acquisition to regular annual inspections and renewal approvals, presents no issues regarding its authenticity and legality. As long as both parties go through the relevant approval procedures in accordance with the relevant local regulations, the fact that the mining right is located in the non-core area of the Reserve does not constitute a substantial obstacle to the subsequent cooperative exploration and development or continued performance of the agreement. Since the two parties signed the agreement and cooperated amicably for over two years, Jinhe Company, while holding the mining right on behalf, has fulfilled its obligations to maintain the mining right as agreed, and the mining right was successfully renewed in April 2013. Meanwhile, Jinhe Company fulfilled its obligation to contribute RMB 2,000,000 for the establishment of the project company as agreed. The project company has now been established, and various work is proceeding in order. The purpose of the contract between the parties is the mineral development of the mining right. To date, no administrative authority has explicitly prohibited the mineral development of the project. Therefore, the parties should continue their friendly cooperation and advance the mineral development work of the mining right.

On December 6, 2013, the Xinjiang Taxkorgan Wildlife Nature Reserve Administration (hereinafter referred to as the Reserve Administration) issued a certificate. The main content was: The Reserve Administration, based on the converted coordinates provided by Jinhe Company from the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region Basic Geographic Information Center for the preliminary survey of the Wuruke Lead Polymetallic Ore in Taxkorgan County, Xinjiang, mapped the coordinates onto the functional zoning map of the Reserve. The areas to which they belong are all within the scope of the Reserve.

Separately found: Lingang Company has paid attorney fees of RMB 200,000 for this lawsuit.

Jinhe Company filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance, alleging: After signing the Cooperation Exploration and Development Agreement with Lingang Company, Lingang Company believed that the cooperative development project was located in the Reserve, violating Article 6.2.3 of the agreement, which states "it is not located within glacier protection areas, nature reserves, scenic spots, or other areas that may affect mining development," and proposed to rescind the agreement. Jinhe Company argued that the agreement was the true expression of the parties' intent and had been actually performed, and the grounds for Lingang Company to rescind the contract at this time are untenable. Jinhe Company requested: 1. To confirm that Lingang Company's act of rescinding the Cooperation Exploration and Development Agreement is invalid; 2. To confirm that the Cooperation Exploration and Development Agreement is valid and that Jinhe Company is not required to refund the RMB 35,000,000 cooperation compensation paid by Lingang Company for the mining right. The litigation costs of this case shall be borne by Lingang Company.

Lingang Company responded in defense: Jinhe Company's claims have no legal basis and should be dismissed. According to the explicit provisions of Articles 6 and 7 of the agreement, the conditions for rescission of the agreement have been met, and Lingang Company's rescission of the contract has a contractual basis. Jinhe Company's second claim is meaningless. Lingang Company has already exercised its right of rescission in accordance with the agreement, and Jinhe Company must return the RMB 35,000,000 cooperation compensation. The litigation costs shall be determined by the court in accordance with law.

Lingang Company filed a counterclaim with the court of first instance, alleging: After the Cooperation Exploration and Development Agreement was signed, Lingang Company performed its relevant contractual obligations in accordance with the agreement. However, Jinhe Company failed to make its representations and warranties in good faith. In 2013, Lingang Company learned that the exploration block under the subject mining right was entirely within the scope of the Reserve. Pursuant to Article 7.1.2 of the agreement, which stipulates that "any party's violation of any representation, warranty, or undertaking made in the agreement, or any representation, warranty, or undertaking made by any party being found to be untrue, inaccurate, or misleading" constitutes a breach of contract, and Article 7.2, which stipulates that "if any party breaches the contract, the other party is entitled to demand immediate termination of this agreement and/or claim liability for breach of contract in accordance with legal provisions, and to seek compensation for all losses incurred thereby (including but not limited to litigation costs, attorney fees, etc.)," Jinhe Company shall bear liability for breach of contract to Lingang Company, including restitution of property and compensation for losses. Lingang Company requested the court to: 1. Rescind the Cooperation Exploration and Development Agreement signed between the parties; 2. Order Jinhe Company to refund the cooperation compensation of RMB 35,000,000 for the mining right to Lingang Company; 3. Order Jinhe Company to compensate Lingang Company for exploration costs of RMB 3,288,150, road construction costs of RMB 5,538,600, mine road access and maintenance costs of RMB 1,500,000, and engineering costs, management costs, etc., of RMB 5,702,257; 4. Order Jinhe Company to compensate Lingang Company for interest losses of RMB 10,843,256.77; 5. Order Jinhe Company to compensate Lingang Company for attorney fees of RMB 429,161.32 and guarantee fees of RMB 700,000, totaling RMB 63,001,425.09. The litigation costs of this case shall be borne by Jinhe Company. After the hearing at first instance, Lingang Company, based on the evidence presented at trial, changed the interest loss in its fourth claim from RMB 10,843,256.77 to RMB 9,465,104.15 and simultaneously withdrew the portion of the guarantee fees of RMB 700,000 in its fifth claim.

Jinhe Company responded in defense: (1) The right to rescind a contract is a right of private relief, which can be exercised by the right holder through a unilateral declaration of intent that requires receipt. Lingang Company's filing of a lawsuit with the court to seek judicial rescission of the signed agreement is procedurally improper. (2) The facts and reasons relied upon by Lingang Company in requesting rescission of the agreement are not objective or sufficient, and its claims cannot be sustained. (a) After the agreement took effect, the parties had actually performed it for two and a half years, and the actual situation of the mine had undergone substantial changes. It is neither objective nor fair for Lingang Company to now request rescission of the agreement. (b) The parties had established the project company as agreed, transferred the mine to the project company, and operated it corporately, with the project company enjoying the rights and bearing the risks. (c) Lingang Company had reviewed the relevant materials of the mine, conducted investigations, evaluations, and field surveys before signing the agreement, and was clearly aware of the specific circumstances of the mine at the time of signing. (d) Jinhe Company's mining right is legal and valid and is not located in a nature reserve or area that may affect mining development, nor does it affect the performance of this agreement. (e) The Reserve was established before the signing of the Cooperation Exploration and Development Agreement, and this fact was publicly known. Hundreds of exploration rights and mining rights have been established within the Reserve, and there are no policy factors affecting the exploration and development of the mine in that area. (f) Jinhe Company has not materially breached the agreement, and there is no fundamental breach that would prevent Lingang Company from achieving the purpose of the contract. Lingang Company has no right to rescind the agreement under the agreement, and its invocation of Article 7.2 of the agreement to claim rescission is erroneous. (g) Lingang Company's attempt to rescind the agreement due to factors such as the contraction of the iron ore market and falling prices is improper and should not be supported. (h) The agreement in question is legally valid, and the stability of the transaction process under this agreement should be maintained. (i) The contractual clause on which Lingang Company bases its claim for rescission was an objective and publicly known fact before the agreement was signed. Lingang Company was aware of this right. Having voluntarily signed the agreement and performed it for two and a half years before filing this lawsuit exceeds the two-year statute of limitations provided by law and should not be protected by law. (j) Lingang Company exercised its right of rescission after two and a half years of signing and performing the agreement, and the time limit has expired, so the request should not be supported.

The court of first instance found that: On October 10, 2011, the Agreement on Cooperative Exploration and Development entered into by Lingang Company and Jinhe Company was a true expression of the parties' intent, and its content did not violate the mandatory or prohibitive provisions of laws and regulations such as the Mineral Resources Law of the PRC, and thus was legally valid. The Agreement had been performed in fact. Lingang Company had paid RMB 35 million to Jinhe Company as agreed. Both parties had jointly funded the establishment of the project company — Tashkurgan County Jinhe Kunlun Resource Investment Co., Ltd. Lingang Company had also entrusted the Geological Survey Institute to conduct geological exploration of the Tie Duo Metal Mine in Wuruk, Tashkurgan County, Xinjiang. Lingang Company did not provide evidence proving that its geological exploration work of the mining rights involved had been affected by adverse factors such as interference or obstruction. From the signing of the Agreement until the filing of the lawsuit, the Agreement had been performed for approximately two and a half years.

(1) Regarding whether the Agreement on Cooperative Exploration and Development at issue should be rescinded. According to the content of the Agreement on Cooperative Exploration and Development, after the Agreement took effect, all subsequent work of general survey, detailed survey, and exploration of the mining rights involved was to be funded and carried out by Lingang Company. Lingang Company undertook to accelerate the exploration work of the mining rights involved immediately after the Agreement was signed, and guaranteed full capital investment for the subsequent stages of general survey, detailed survey, and exploration. Jinhe Company, in turn, undertook that the mining rights involved would not be located in areas such as glacier protection zones, nature reserves, scenic areas, or other regions that might affect mine development. If the Agreement could not be performed due to force majeure, the Agreement would terminate upon written confirmation by both parties; if one party materially breached the Agreement, preventing the other party from achieving the purpose of the Agreement, the non-breaching party had the right to rescind the Agreement. According to the certificate issued by the Reserve Management Bureau on December 6, 2013, the entire area of the mining rights involved was within the reserve. Both Jinhe Company and Lingang Company acknowledged the fact that the area of the mining rights involved was within the reserve, and that the reserve had been established prior to the signing of the contract. Government authorities, when establishing a reserve, should publicize relevant information and materials about the reserve, which constitute public information accessible to all. Therefore, both parties to this case should have known the fact that the mining rights involved were within the reserve before signing the contract. Although the mining rights involved were located within the reserve, during the more than two years of performance of the contract, Lingang Company did not raise any objection to Jinhe Company, nor did it provide evidence to show that its exploration work had been affected. The term "may affect" as stipulated in Article 6 of the Agreement did not specify the specific content of such impact, constituting an ambiguity in the agreement. Article 11 of the Agreement stipulated: "If the contract cannot be performed due to force majeure, the Agreement shall terminate upon confirmation by both parties; if one party's material breach prevents the other party from achieving the purpose of the contract, the other party has the right to rescind the contract." Jinhe Company did not have any material breach as referred to in the said stipulation, nor was it sufficient to render the purpose of the contract unattainable. Thus, the contract at issue did not present any circumstances as agreed by the parties that would warrant termination or rescission. Therefore, the court of first instance, in accordance with law, granted Lingang Company's claim to confirm that Jinhe Company's rescission of the Agreement at issue was invalid, and did not grant Lingang Company's counterclaim for rescission of the Agreement on Cooperative Exploration and Development.

(2) Regarding the issue of RMB 35 million. Jinhe Company acknowledged receipt of the RMB 35 million payment from Lingang Company. From the content of the Agreement on Cooperative Exploration and Development at issue, the amount as agreed by the parties should be a compensation payment for the cooperation of mining rights. Although Article 4 of the Agreement described and stipulated this amount as a deposit, based on Lingang Company's bank transfer payment certificate and the receipt issued by Jinhe Company, neither indicated it was a deposit. Moreover, Article 2 of Lingang Company's counterclaim explicitly sought the return of the compensation payment for mining rights cooperation. The above facts demonstrate that both parties to the contract regarded this amount as a compensation payment for mining rights cooperation, not a deposit. Therefore, the court of first instance, in accordance with law, confirmed this amount as the cooperation compensation payment paid by Lingang Company to Jinhe Company. Since the contract was not rescinded, the court of first instance did not grant Lingang Company's counterclaim for Jinhe Company to return the cooperation compensation payment of RMB 35 million. Jinhe Company's claim that it was not required to refund the compensation payment already paid by Lingang Company was encompassed within its claim to confirm that Lingang Company's rescission of the Agreement at issue was invalid and did not require a separate assertion. Therefore, the court of first instance did not include this claim in the judgment items.

(3) Regarding Lingang Company's claimed losses: exploration expenses of RMB 3,288,150, road construction expenses of RMB 5,538,600, mine road maintenance fees of RMB 1,500,000, engineering and management expenses of RMB 5,702,257, interest losses of RMB 9,465,104.15, and attorney's fees of RMB 429,161.32. The above counterclaims of Lingang Company were all based on the rescission of the contract at issue. Since the contract was not rescinded, the court of first instance did not grant the above counterclaims of Lingang Company.

In summary, pursuant to Articles 8 and 60 of the Contract Law of the PRC, Article 152 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, and Article 2 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Evidence in Civil Proceedings, the court of first instance rendered the following judgment: 1. Lingang Company's rescission of the Agreement on Cooperative Exploration and Development was invalid; Lingang Company and Jinhe Company shall continue to perform the Agreement on Cooperative Exploration and Development signed on October 10, 2011; 2. Lingang Company's counterclaim was dismissed. The court acceptance fee for the main action was RMB 100, to be borne by Lingang Company. The court acceptance fee for the counterclaim was RMB 356,807.13, to be borne by Lingang Company.

Lingang Company, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed to this Court, alleging: (1) Jinhe Company breached the Agreement on Cooperative Exploration and Development, and the purpose of the contract could not be achieved due to its breach; Lingang Company had the right to rescind the contract in accordance with the Contract Law of the PRC and the terms of the Agreement. The judgment of first instance erroneously found that Jinhe Company had no breach and that the purpose of the contract was not frustrated and should be corrected. (2) Since Lingang Company had the right to rescind the Agreement on Cooperative Exploration and Development, Jinhe Company should return the corresponding payments and compensate for losses. The court of first instance erred in not granting Lingang Company's related claims and should be corrected. Requests: 1. Set aside items (1) and (2) of the civil judgment (2014) Xin Min Er Chu Zi No. 13; 2. Amend the judgment to rescind the Agreement on Cooperative Exploration and Development signed by both parties; 3. Amend the judgment to order Jinhe Company to return the mining rights cooperation compensation payment of RMB 35 million to Lingang Company; 4. Amend the judgment to order Jinhe Company to compensate Lingang Company for exploration expenses of RMB 3,288,150, road construction expenses of RMB 5,538,600, mine road maintenance fees of RMB 1,500,000, and engineering and management expenses of RMB 5,702,257; 5. Amend the judgment to order Jinhe Company to pay Lingang Company interest losses, calculated at the same-period same-type bank loan interest rate, on the cooperation compensation payment of RMB 35 million from the actual date of receipt by Jinhe Company (October 25, 2011) until the actual date of repayment; on other losses from the date Lingang Company proposed rescission (November 22, 2013) until the actual date of repayment; 6. Amend the judgment to order Jinhe Company to compensate Lingang Company for first-instance attorney's fees of RMB 200,000; 7. Order Jinhe Company to compensate Lingang Company for second-instance attorney's fees of RMB 500,000; 8. Order Jinhe Company to bear all litigation costs of the first and second instances.

Jinhe Company responded: (1) Jinhe Company was not at fault and had no material breach; it did not affect the achievement of the purpose of the Agreement on Cooperative Exploration and Development. Lingang Company had no right to rescind the Agreement. The findings of the first-instance judgment were objective and fair. (2) Lingang Company should continue to perform the Agreement in accordance with law and contract. Its request for return of the mining rights cooperation compensation payment and compensation for alleged losses was untenable. Requested that Lingang Company's appeal be dismissed.

During the second instance, Lingang Company submitted the following new evidence: New Evidence 1: a plan view and a satellite map showing the exploration area and the location of the nature reserve, intended to prove that the exploration area at issue was within the reserve. New Evidence 2: the agency agreement and an attorney's fee invoice, intended to prove that Lingang Company incurred RMB 500,000 in second-instance attorney's fees due to this case. New Evidence 3: a CD video and a transcript of the video conversation, intended to prove that since 2012, Tashkurgan County had not permitted the establishment of any mining development enterprises.

Jinhe Company, in cross-examination of the new evidence submitted by Lingang Company, argued: The coordinates in New Evidence 1 differed from those held by Jinhe Company and should be based on the exploration license and the coordinates on the website of the Department of Land and Resources of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region. The attorney's fees in New Evidence 2 were a unilateral civil act by Lingang Company and should not be borne by Jinhe Company. The source of the video in New Evidence 3 was irregular and subject to uncertainty, not satisfying the three elements of evidence, and could not prove the intended purpose.

During the second instance, Jinhe Company submitted the following new evidence: New Evidence 1: the detailed survey exploration license for the Wuruk iron mine in Tashkurgan County, Xinjiang (License No. T65120081202022682), intended to prove that the validity of the mining rights involved had been extended to May 19, 2017, was legally valid, and capable of continued cooperative exploration and development. New Evidence 2: a notice from the Department of Land and Resources of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region titled "Notice on Issuing the Project Task Book for the 2015 Central Return of Two-Rights Proceeds for Mineral Survey and Evaluation (First Batch)", intended to prove that in 2015, the Central and Xinjiang local governments continued to increase investment and operations in mineral exploration and development within the reserve area, and the Geological Survey Institute continued to undertake mineral survey and evaluation projects in the area. New Evidence 3: a functional zoning map of the reserve and a distribution map of some mining rights in the area with related explanations, intended to prove that there were hundreds of exploration rights and mining rights within the reserve, that Lingang Company held other mining rights it had already acquired in the area, and that the mining rights under cooperation were located in the experimental zone and the buffer zone, not affecting the cooperative exploration and development or the achievement of the contract purpose. New Evidence 4: a set of site photos, intended to prove that after the contract was signed, road construction and machinery mobilization took place, and the Agreement on Cooperative Exploration and Development had been performed for more than two years.

Lingang Company, in cross-examination of the new evidence submitted by Jinhe Company, argued: The authenticity of New Evidence 1 was recognized, but its legality and evidentiary purpose were not recognized. According to relevant regulations, no mineral resource exploration or development was permitted within nature reserves, raising doubt as to whether the competent authority should have issued this license. The authenticity of New Evidence 2 could not be confirmed, and its relevance and evidentiary purpose were not recognized. The document did not include the mining rights at issue, and the return of two-rights proceeds by the central finance could not prove the legality of mineral exploration and development. New Evidence 3 was prepared unilaterally by Jinhe Company; the accuracy of its content could not be confirmed; its authenticity and evidentiary purpose were not recognized. Whether the exploration area was in the experimental zone or the buffer zone of the nature reserve lacked a reliable third-party source. The authenticity of the eight site photos in New Evidence 4 was doubtful, and the first photo was taken before the signing of the Agreement between the parties; these photos reflected the harsh natural conditions in the area, and the roads and bridges constructed could corroborate Lingang Company's losses.

This Court, in evaluating the new evidence submitted by Lingang Company, finds: New Evidence 1 (plan and satellite map) was prepared unilaterally by Lingang Company; Jinhe Company did not recognize it; its objectivity could not be determined and it is not admitted. New Evidence 2 (agency agreement and attorney's fee payment voucher) — Jinhe Company did not object to its authenticity and did not submit sufficient rebuttal evidence; it is admitted. The authenticity of New Evidence 3 (video and its transcript) cannot be determined and is not admitted.

This Court, in evaluating the new evidence submitted by Jinhe Company, finds: The authenticity of New Evidence 1 (exploration license) was not disputed by Lingang Company; it is admitted. New Evidence 2 (document from the local Land and Resources Department) is not relevant to this case and is not admitted. New Evidence 3 (maps and related explanations) was prepared unilaterally by Jinhe Company; Lingang Company did not recognize it; its objectivity and authenticity cannot be determined and it is not admitted. The authenticity of New Evidence 4 (photos) cannot be determined and is not admitted.

This Court confirms the facts found by the court of first instance.

This Court holds: The dispute in the second instance focuses on: (1) whether the Agreement on Cooperative Exploration and Development entered into by Lingang Company and Jinhe Company should be rescinded; (2) whether Lingang Company's request for Jinhe Company to return the cooperation compensation payment and compensate for input losses can be established.

(1) Regarding whether the Agreement on Cooperative Exploration and Development at issue should be rescinded.

The exploration right under the Agreement on Cooperative Exploration and Development is located within the Tashkurgan Wildlife Nature Reserve in Xinjiang. The nature reserve was established first, and Jinhe Company's exploration right was obtained later. From the stipulation in Article 6.2.3 of the Agreement that "Party B guarantees that the exploration certificate obtained ... will not be located in areas such as glacier protection zones, nature reserves, scenic areas, or other regions that may affect mine development," both parties knew or should have known that exploration and development of mineral resources are not permitted within nature reserves. Article 26 of the Regulations on Nature Reserves of the PRC prohibits activities such as felling, grazing, hunting, fishing, gathering medicinal herbs, reclamation, burning, mining, quarrying, and sand digging within nature reserves. Jinhe Company argued that although the mining rights at issue were within the nature reserve, they were located in the experimental zone and the buffer zone, where exploration is legally permitted. Article 18 of the Regulations on Nature Reserves of the PRC provides: "Nature reserves can be divided into core zones, buffer zones, and experimental zones. Areas within nature reserves that have well-preserved natural ecosystems and concentrated distributions of rare and endangered flora and fauna should be designated as core zones, where no individual or unit is allowed to enter; except with approval in accordance with Article 27 of these Regulations, entry for scientific research activities is also not permitted. A certain area of buffer zone may be designated around the core zone, where entry is only permitted for scientific research and observation activities. The area outside the buffer zone shall be designated as the experimental zone, where entry is permitted for activities such as scientific experiments, teaching internships, visits and inspections, tourism, and domestication and breeding of rare and endangered wildlife." Jinhe Company argued that exploration falls within the scope of "such other activities." This Court is of the opinion that mining is explicitly prohibited under Article 26 of the Regulations on Nature Reserves of the PRC and clearly does not fall within the activities permitted under Article 18 of the same Regulations. Jinhe Company's argument lacks legal basis and cannot be sustained. Therefore, the Agreement on Cooperative Exploration and Development entered into by the parties violates the prohibitive provisions of the Regulations on Nature Reserves of the PRC. If the Agreement were recognized as valid and continued to be performed, it would cause serious damage to the natural environment and ecology, harming the public interest concerning the environment. According to Articles 52, paragraphs (4) and (5) of the Contract Law of the PRC, the Agreement on Cooperative Exploration and Development should be void. The court of first instance erroneously found the Agreement valid and ordered the parties to continue performance, which was an erroneous application of law. This Court corrects this error. Since a void contract does not involve rescission, both Jinhe Company's claim for a declaration that Lingang Company's rescission of the Agreement on Cooperative Exploration and Development was invalid and Lingang Company's counterclaim for rescission of the Agreement on Cooperative Exploration and Development are not granted.

(2) Regarding the determination of returning property and compensating losses.

Article 58 of the Contract Law of the PRC provides: "After a contract is void or rescinded, property acquired as a result of the contract shall be returned; if return is impossible or unnecessary, the value shall be compensated. The party at fault shall compensate the other party for losses thus incurred; if both parties are at fault, each party shall bear corresponding liability." Since the Agreement on Cooperative Exploration and Development is void, Jinhe Company shall return the cooperation compensation payment of RMB 35 million paid by Lingang Company to Jinhe Company under the Agreement. During the performance of the Agreement on Cooperative Exploration and Development, Lingang Company entered into a "Road Construction Project Contract" and a "Supplementary Contract" with Kashi Regional Highway and Bridge Engineering Co., Ltd. for constructing roads for the exploration project at issue. The roads have become part of the mining area property and should be compensated by Jinhe Company. Of the construction costs paid by Lingang Company, RMB 2.5 million is evidenced by payment vouchers bearing bank seals, which is sufficient evidence. This Court supports this claim. The remaining road construction costs of RMB 3,038,600, as well as the exploration expenses of RMB 3,288,150 and mine road maintenance fees of RMB 1,500,000 claimed by Lingang Company, are supported by payment vouchers that are electronic receipts printed by Lingang Company without bank stamps for confirmation. Jinhe Company, during cross-examination in the first instance, argued that electronic receipts can be printed by oneself but should be stamped by the bank for confirmation, and its authenticity was not recognized. Lingang Company did not supplement evidence on this point in the second instance, and the authenticity of its payment vouchers cannot be determined. This Court does not admit them. The engineering and management expenses of RMB 5,702,257 claimed by Lingang Company are expenses incurred in the daily operation and management of the project company, and the payor was the project company. Since both Lingang Company and Jinhe Company made capital contributions when the project company was established, these expenses cannot be solely attributed to Lingang Company's losses. This portion should be resolved separately during the liquidation of the project company. Lingang Company, before the cooperation, failed to conduct a necessary investigation into the location of the mining area and invested blindly. It is at fault for the voidness of the Agreement on Cooperative Exploration and Development and should bear the resulting loss of interest on its own. Therefore, its claim for interest losses of approximately RMB 6,653,300 is not granted. Lingang Company's claim for attorney's fees is based on Article 7.2 of the Agreement on Cooperative Exploration and Development. Since the Agreement is now found void, attorney's fees shall be borne by Lingang Company. Jinhe Company's exploration right remains in its own name, and there is no issue of return. Lingang Company shall return the management authority of the mine to Jinhe Company. If Jinhe Company suffers losses due to the voidness of the Agreement on Cooperative Exploration and Development, it may assert its rights in a separate action.

In summary, the judgment of first instance had clear findings of fact but an erroneous application of law, which should be corrected. This Court, pursuant to Article 170, paragraph 1(2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, renders the following judgment:

1. The civil judgment (2014) Xin Min Er Chu Zi No. 13 of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region is set aside;

2. The "Agreement on Cooperative Exploration and Development of General Survey Exploration Rights for the Wuruk Lead Polymetallic Mine in Tashkurgan County, Xinjiang" entered into by Xinjiang Lingang Resource Investment Co., Ltd. and Sichuan Jinhe Mining Co., Ltd. is void;

3. Sichuan Jinhe Mining Co., Ltd. shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, return the mining rights cooperation compensation payment of RMB 35 million to Xinjiang Lingang Resource Investment Co., Ltd.;

4. Sichuan Jinhe Mining Co., Ltd. shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, compensate Xinjiang Lingang Resource Investment Co., Ltd. for road construction expenses of RMB 2.5 million;

5. The claims of Sichuan Jinhe Mining Co., Ltd. are dismissed;

6. Dismiss all other claims of Xinjiang Lingang Resources Investment Co., Ltd.

If the obligation to pay money is not performed within the period specified in this judgment, the interest on the debt during the period of delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

The court acceptance fee for the original action in the first instance is RMB 100, and for the counterclaim is RMB 356,807.13, to be borne equally by Jinhe Company and Lingang Company, each paying RMB 178,453.565. The acceptance fee for the second instance is RMB 333,711.54, to be borne equally by Jinhe Company and Lingang Company, each paying RMB 166,855.77.

This judgment is final.
